22

  • N: nīš ilīšu | kabta | qalliš | izkuru | anāku | amšal
  • T: Who casually swore a solemn oath by his god: I, indeed, became like (such a one)!
  • L: nīš ← nīšu II “(oath on the) life nīš ili(m), ilāni, DN, *šarri(m)…”; ilīšu ← ilu I, -šu I “pl. ilū, ilānu god, deity a or the god, also du.”; kabta ← kabtu I “f. kabittu(m) heavy”; qalliš ← qalliš I “lightly jB”; izkuru ← zakāru I “to speak, say”; anāku ← anāku I “I”; amšal ← mašālu I “to equal”
  • Note: [RN3311: 51] suggests the reading am-rak instead of am-šal on account of vowel class of the verb mašālu (not a verb of the a/a-class according to Borger; see also [RN2721: M/1 355] and [RN862hh: 82]). In [RN2720: 623], three different vowel classes are considered possible for mašālu, depending on the dialect (u/u for OB/SB, a/a for SB and i/i for MB). Therefore, the vowel in the preterite form does not seem to be a sufficient reason to determine the correct reading of the verb. The verb mašālu is favored here because it fits the overall structure of the passage: the verb at the end of this line is connected to the prepositions kīma/kī (l. 12) and ana (l. 21), and both of these prepositions can be used with mašālu to indicate the object of resemblance (see [RN2721: M/1 355-356]). See also the discussion in [RN1402: 66].
